name: v90_batch_gen9
_why: Supersedes runs/spsa/v90_guessed_params, which was configured against
sgr_v9_rc.exe and gen8 -- both pre-date the v9.0 release. It reached
iteration 275 before gen9 datagen took the machine.
Not the shipped binary: sgr_v9_0.exe advertises all ten options but eight of
them are compiled out at HEAD (SGR_IIR, SGR_NMPSCALE, SGR_RAZOR, SGR_FUTILITY,
SGR_SEEPRUNE, SGR_HISTPRUNE, SGR_CAPHIST all 0). SPSA shares one match result
across every parameter, so eight dead dimensions would add noise to the two
live ones. The engine below is HEAD with all nine batch toggles on: bench 12
Hash pinned at 256 to match pool calibration. The earlier run left it at the
48 MB default -- symmetric, so unbiased, but METHODOLOGY 9 is a 45 Elo
correction caused by unpinned hash, so don't leave the gap.
Time-management parameters excluded on purpose. METHODOLOGY 6: the v3.1 soft
limit measured +24.6 self-play and negative pooled.

params.name: HistLmrDiv
params._note: Suspect #1. Shipped inert at 400000 for four versions; 128 was picked off a measured |hist| distribution, never off games. Range is 16..2000000, so c is set by hand rather than from the range.

params.name: HistPruneMargin
params._note: Suspect #2. Never behaved like a pruner at any swept setting.

params.name: CapHistMax
params._note: The clamp that makes capture history structurally safe. 256 was reasoned from MVV-LVA tier spacing, not measured.

params.name: RazorMargin
params._note: Only value swept where razoring pruned at all; the neighbours went non-monotonic.

params.name: LmrDivX100
params._note: Not new, and never swept either -- the 2.5 divisor has been hand-set since v1.0.
